purpose: Functional verification of Rust scroll-thumb geometry, drag state and Metal ownership; not a performance benchmark

bundle_signature.mode: unchanged repository packager and configured permanent certificate

verified_mechanisms: Rust computes normalized content offset, maximum range, minimum thumb length and both track endpoints. The native ScrollBar measurement/bounds adapter applies the returned geometry after native metric updates and on layout.

Rust stores the pointer grip and initial content offset across capture. Dragging maps track coordinates to the current content range, clamps endpoints, preserves the 128-point cross-axis snap-back policy and normalizes content shrink. Release/capture loss cancel the Rust state.

The existing Metal canvas now includes the vertical scrollbar gutter. A clipped Rust display primitive draws the inset thumb; platform color-provider normal/hover/pressed colors remain adapters. There is no second Metal layer, queue or renderer.

Native thumb painting is gated while Metal is visible. The fallback draws the same Rust primitive through the native canvas; ownership, animation, swipe and drawable-failure paths request fresh native scrollbar paint.

The opt-in backend replaces the fading Cocoa scrollbar with an always-visible overflow thumb. No fading timer or animation polling is introduced. The default Views backend retains its original scrollbar.

Native ScrollView scrolling, wheel/gesture delivery, ScrollBar track repeat, menu and key dispatch remain adapters. The new native accessibility node exposes its name, numeric range/current value and increment/decrement actions.

The new browser regression physically drags to the end, moves outside the snap threshold, returns and releases capture; submitted thumb geometry matches the native hit target. It also clicks the track, dispatches Home/End and invokes accessibility decrement.

The bitmap regression confirms no native thumb ink under Metal and restores native ink with the panel hidden. Existing real wheel/scroll/tab selection, fractional viewport, large sidebar, input, split/folder/session and settings regressions pass.
New Tab canvas bounds now explicitly include the scrollbar while preserving its viewport-aligned action width.
manual_observations: The matching signed and timestamped app showed the GPU thumb alongside real Unicode tabs, with the original split pair and address/heading visible.

Accessibility Increment changed the scrollbar value from 0 to 122 and moved the list. Scrolling reached value 328 with tab 24 visible at the bottom; selecting it opened the correct real Chromium page.
Scrolling back returned the accessibility value to 0; selecting the original first pair member restored the split view. The prototype was closed and its launcher exited successfully.

A separate CUA element-index right click opened the sidebar background menu rather than supplying reliable scrollbar-menu evidence; it was dismissed and that prototype run was closed. No product change was inferred from this coordinate-routing observation.
The normal application/profile was not used.
limitations: The scrollbar now stays visible while content overflows; Cocoa fading/expansion appearance is intentionally replaced in this prototype.

Native ScrollBar/View nodes, range bookkeeping, track autorepeat, menu and keyboard dispatch, wheel/fling services and accessibility delivery remain. This is not complete Views scroll-container removal.

The new native regression verifies track, drag, key adapter and AX behavior but does not independently exercise the scrollbar context menu. Its inherited menu/controller binding still needs dedicated native input coverage.
Horizontal workspace scrolling, footer/navigation painting, resize/autohide, split headers, animations and the remaining forms/palettes still require migration.
This is not a complete VoiceOver/trackpad/RTL/scale matrix or a CPU/GPU/physical-presentation speed comparison.
No new third-party binary dependency was introduced; original-code Apache-2.0 and required upstream notices are unchanged.
